title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy as a Driver of Trust, Fairness, and Evidence Appraisal in Public Health Decision-Making
venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
abstract: Systems of artificial intelligence (AI) are now being widely adopted in public health, affecting the evidence generation and decision-making processes. We are now in a new age, marked not only by innovation and progress but also by how technology is perceived. Although the outcomes of AI research are not always consistent, we can at least ensure that AI is fair and gain a clearer understanding of how the results of AI research could inform each country's approach to empowering its citizens through literacy. From this perspective, concerns about data interpretation and the ethics of accountability in the governance of AI systems in healthcare are conceivably mitigating risks related to health inequities in global healthcare systems. The proposed strategy will address AI literacy and take a holistic approach to its various domains.
